_comment:
Derived from what the corpus actually contains, not from what would be convenient. In 40 real SWE-agent trajectories the only high-frequency mutable entity is the file under edit: 21 distinct paths across 146 mentions, with the agent moving between them. Last-write-wins is exactly right for that -- an agent works on one file at a time -- and a 30-turn-deep session genuinely needs to be told which one is current.

Two properties were arrived at by measuring precision, not by taste:
(1) paths are almost always wrapped in markdown backticks or quotes, so a pattern assuming bare whitespace between the trigger and the path matches almost nothing;
(2) a weak trigger like 'in <path>' matches prose, and was the sole source of every incorrect label in the first precision pass. Both alternatives below require an explicit verb naming an action on the file.

current_file: \b(?:working on|changes (?:to|in)|making changes (?:to|in)|should be editing|need(?:ed)? to edit(?: the)?|instead of)\s+(?:^|[\s`'\"/(])([\w][\w./-]*\.(?:py|js|ts|tsx|jsx|go|rs|java|rb|cpp|hpp))\b

value_contracts.corpus_note: read_path_* counts what the read path can see: customer and agent turns, minus tool output and minus an agent turn listing its options; in_tool_output is what those exclusions cost

current_file.basis: structure from the slot's own capture group
current_file.derived_from: the slot's own entity patterns; see contextgc/value_shapes.py

failing_test.basis: structure from the slot's own capture group
failing_test.derived_from: the slot's own entity patterns; see contextgc/value_shapes.py

failing_test.why: the pattern's own boundary is looser than this case needs

_measurement.precision_note: The combined figure, because the console shows one number and it has to be the one that covers the whole label set: 90% over 130 independent units from 142 rows. Per slot the two are not the same and neither is the headline: current_file 98% (n=98), failing_test 75% (n=44). Showing 98% because it is the better slot is the same flattering-staleness this file was corrected for, with a fresh number. A previous revision said '100% (n=36)' with failing_test unlabelled; the labels arrived, the slot turned out to be four times worse than the one beside it, and the 100% was a statement about one regex rather than about the schema. PROVENANCE: these 142 labels were collected from a worksheet built before the loader fix, on load_swe_agent(limit=6000) with per_repo=None. That window cannot be reproduced by the default CLI, which caps per_repo at 2, so this figure is only reproducible on the window named here. Worksheets built now load the CLI's own defaults and will match the report.
